tasks.task: Map a team's tasks and score each for AI fit

items.when: Before scoring, to break each role into the real tasks it does in a week
When tasks are listed and each needs a score for fit, time at stake, risk and data
When the map comes from what managers say and nobody has watched the work being done
When a top candidate looks too good, to test it three ways before it goes on the shortlist
When a task also trains juniors or catches errors, to see what would be lost
When you want a second verdict on whether one process should be automated at all

tasks.task: Redesign one process with AI steps and human checks

items.when: Before the redesign, to get today's steps mapped with the bottlenecks ranked
When each new step must be marked AI, tool or person, with the full prompt for AI steps
When the process is long, to compare a design that splits it across several agents
When a redesigned workflow disappoints, to rank its weak points and their causes
Before the team relies on it, to find double runs, missing approvals and silent failures

tasks.task: Write a one-page staff AI use policy

items.when: When staff need allowed uses, data that never goes in and who approves new tools on one page
When you want a second draft built from public model policies, to compare
When a rule guards against small slips but not the one leak that would end a client
When any allowed use touches staff data, to shorten the data list and draft a notice
When the page reads like a legal notice and staff will not follow it

tasks.task: Compare the AI tools on a shortlist

items.when: When the shortlist is not set yet and you need the right kind of tool for each job
When two to four tools or plans need a fair side-by-side on the team's own tasks
When you want scored criteria, a trial plan and a cost view to test your pick
When ChatGPT is on the shortlist and you need what it does and where it falls short
When Claude is on the shortlist and you need what it does and where it falls short
When the team lives in Word, Excel and Outlook and Copilot is on the shortlist
When the team uses Google's apps and Gemini is on the shortlist

tasks.task: Plan a 30-day AI pilot with go and stop rules

items.when: When a team starts with AI, or has licences nobody uses, to run the steps in order
When two or three tasks are chosen and the pilot needs a baseline, a check and stop rules
Before the pilot plan is fixed, to compare two plans that bet the 30 days and the budget differently
Before the pilot starts, to confirm the task passes and to set a first small test
When the success rules are a long scorecard and one simple rule would decide it better

tasks.task: Review AI pilot results and make a go or stop call

items.when: Before judging, to find gaps and odd values in the pilot's time and error log
When the pilot has ended and the owner needs a call based on the rules agreed at the start
When results must be set against the baseline and a go or stop checklist with evidence
When you must weigh results against costs and harms: grow, limit, change or stop
When you want the evidence brief and data gaps reviewed before the owner sees them
When everyone liked the pilot and the numbers are being read to fit that feeling

tasks.task: Run a data and risk check on one AI use

items.when: When someone wants AI for one task and you must decide fast: yes, yes with rules, or no
When the use affects people's work or outcomes and needs risks and conditions written up
When personal data goes in and a fuller privacy assessment is needed
When the business works in the EU and the use may fall into a regulated risk tier

tasks.task: Build and review the register of AI tools in use

items.when: When nobody knows which AI tools are paid for, to list them from the bills first
When each tool needs an owner, the data allowed in it and a review date
Every three months, or straight after an incident or a change in a vendor's data terms
When the firm sells or works in the EU and needs a first read of its duties
When a client or auditor asks how AI is managed and the gaps must be found

tasks.task: Check an AI vendor before buying or renewing

items.when: Before a team signs up, renews, or lets a tool connect to email, files or a CRM
When you have the vendor's terms and need data-training and liability risks flagged
When the tool will read staff data and needs a privacy review and a notice

tasks.task: Tell staff about new AI rules or an approved tool

items.when: When new rules or a newly approved tool must be explained calmly with an FAQ
When some staff will push back, to compare message options and a plan for objections
When the approved policy needs a plain explanation of what changes for each person
A few weeks later, to see if staff follow the rules and what stands in the way

tasks.task: Build a tested team prompt library

items.when: When a staff member's rough prompt must become one clear prompt worth sharing
When each entry needs testing on samples, with an example and a check, before it is shared
When two versions of a prompt compete, to score both on the same test cases
When an important prompt needs real tests and a version history
Each month, to find weak, clashing or unsafe entries in the shared library

tasks.task: Plan a two-hour hands-on AI workshop

items.when: When a team has licences but no training and needs practice on its own weekly tasks
When you want a second outline built from one real work problem, to compare
When practice rounds are free play and each should drill one habit with feedback
When the session needs a one-page handout people still use a month later
A few weeks after, to compare real work with the skills check taken before

tasks.task: Write a build spec for the automated steps

items.when: When one repeated task needs laying out step by step with what can break
When the steps will run in Zapier or Make and must hold up, or need code instead
When a developer will build it and needs every path, failure and test case written
When the client will run the flow in Make and you must check what it can connect
When the build is done, to test for double runs and steps with no approval

tasks.task: Run a first AI rollout for a small team

items.when: When staff use free tools with client data, or bought licences sit unused
When the rollout needs its rules and tool register written before anyone is trained
When the people side is the risk: who is affected, who resists and what to say when
After a month, to see who uses the tools and the rules and who does not

tasks.task: Write a safe-use cheat sheet and a follow-up micro-course

items.when: Before writing, to take the habits and practice tasks the workshop taught
When the rules must fit one page staff keep at their desk
When the follow-up could be a short web course with lessons and quizzes, not emails
When the course should teach one checking habit staff use after every AI answer
When the cheat sheet uses AI jargon office staff would not

tasks.task: Set how staff check AI output before it is used

items.when: When the policy says check outputs and staff need to know how for each kind of task
When an AI answer states facts that will go to a client, to check each against sources
When a repeated task needs a scoring guide so checks are the same every time
When staff accept answers too fast and need one quick doubt step each time

tasks.task: Test and tune a prompt or chatbot

items.when: When you have a prompt and test cases and need scores for each version
When a prompt gives uneven answers and needs tightening before it is tested again
When the bot's flow is the problem: questions, recovery from mistakes and handover
When answers must be graded the same way every time and you need the scoring guide

tasks.task: Check an AI assistant or agent for misuse and runaway cost

items.when: When an AI app reads outside text and needs defences, tests and spending caps
When the assistant reads emails or web pages that could carry hidden instructions
When the client owns the agent and wants a safe test of where it can be tricked
When the agent can act through tools and needs limits on permissions and risky actions
When the monthly bill surprises the owner and you must find where it goes

tasks.task: Review an AI mistake and update the rules

items.when: When an AI mistake reached a client and needs a blame-free report and a safer procedure
Straight after the incident, to review the tool's entry and the rules around it
When the use that failed must be checked again before it is allowed to restart
When the rule change that follows must be told to staff without blame

tasks.task: Turn an expert's know-how into a shared assistant

items.when: When the team's best person holds the judgment and it must be asked out with real cases
When their way of working should become a prompt, skill or agent others can use
When the assistant exists and needs test cases and a judge that grades as the expert would

tasks.task: Advise whether to build, buy or wait on an AI idea

items.when: Before any spend, to check the problem is one AI can really help with
When the owner is choosing between a ready tool, an API and a custom build
When the choice is close, to lay out two plans with the money and dates showing and recommend one
When there are early results, to weigh them against cost and harm before spending more
When the forecast is uncertain and a simple rule of thumb beats a detailed model

always.when: Before any report states what a tool does with data, to check it against the vendor's own terms

helpers.when: When the redesigned workflow must be built and run in Zapier, Make or n8n
When one prompt carries real risk and needs a full test set and tuning
When the AI rules must be checked against privacy law or a regulator's guidance
When licences, sign-in, sharing settings or connectors must be changed in the tools
When one workshop must grow into a training programme for the whole firm
When the chosen use is a customer-facing bot that must be built and tested

gaps: No library item scores a team's tasks for AI fit, time at stake, risk and data sensitivity in one map; only the kit does
No library item writes a 30-day pilot plan with a baseline and go and stop rules; the library covers only the review after
No library item builds a register of AI tools with owner, data allowed, approval and review date
No library item gives a quick data and risk check for one AI use in a small firm; the assessments are full legal-style ones
No library item lists the questions to ask an AI vendor on training, retention and sub-processors
No library item compares business plans of chat assistants on data terms, admin controls and price
No library item plans a hands-on AI workshop from a team's own tasks or runs a before and after skills check
No library item sets up a shared prompt library with owners and a test for each entry
No library item writes the staff message and FAQ for new AI rules, or reviews an AI mistake as its own kind of incident
No library item covers rolling out Copilot or Gemini in a workplace: admin settings and files shared too widely
No library item finds which AI tools staff already use without approval
No library item measures time saved by an AI step with a timing log before and after
No library item says when and how to tell customers that AI was used
